/-!
# Conjecture 8.21

by L. G. Kovács

If the commutator subgroup $G'$ of a relatively free group $G$ is periodic, must $G'$ have
finite exponent?

A group is *relatively free* if it is free in some variety of groups. Equivalently, it has a
generating set $X$ such that every map $X \to G$ extends to an endomorphism of $G$
(H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1). No restriction is placed on the rank of $G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup / IsFreeGroup (only absolutely free groups, far too narrow); Subgroup.closure, MonoidHom (used as building blocks); Monoid.IsTorsion and Monoid.ExponentExists (used for 'periodic' and 'finite exponent').
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.21».IsRelativelyFree
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has any notion of a variety of groups, verbal subgroup, or relatively free group (searched for 'relatively free', 'variety of groups', 'RelativelyFree', 'GroupVariety', 'IsVariety'). Defined as: G has a generating set X (Subgroup.closure X = ⊤) such that every map X → G extends to a monoid hom G →* G. This is the standard characterisation of 'free in some variety of groups' (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups, Ch. 1), and is the reading given in the decomposition notes. Two short proved API lemmas (FreeGroup α and subsingleton groups are relatively free) test the definition.

blocks.name: IsRelativelyFree
blocks.text:
/--
A group $G$ is *relatively free* (that is, free in some variety of groups) if it has a
generating set $X$ such that every map $X \to G$ extends to an endomorphism of $G$.
-/
def IsRelativelyFree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Set G, Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ f : X → G, ∃ φ : G →* G, ∀ x : X, φ x = f x

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_freeGroup (α : Type*) : IsRelativelyFree (FreeGroup α) := by
  refine ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, fun f => ?_⟩
  refine ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun a => f ⟨FreeGroup.of a, a, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨_, a, rfl⟩
  simp

theorem isRelativelyFree_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsRelativelyFree G :=
  ⟨∅, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun _ => ⟨MonoidHom.id G, fun x => x.2.elim⟩⟩

blocks.docstring:
If the commutator subgroup $G'$ of a relatively free group $G$ is periodic, must $G'$ have
finite exponent?

Here "periodic" means that every element of $G'$ has finite order, and "finite exponent"
means that there is some $n \geq 1$ with $x^n = 1$ for all $x \in G'$.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, implicitly universally quantified over all relatively free groups G of arbitrary (possibly infinite) rank, i.e. groups free in some variety of groups (equivalently, G has a generating set every map of which into G extends to an endomorphism); 'periodic' means every element of G' has finite order (IsTorsion) and 'finite exponent' means some n ≥ 1 with x^n = 1 for all x ∈ G' (Monoid.ExponentExists), so the Prop is ∀ relatively free G, IsTorsion G' → ExponentExists G', stated as answer(sorry) ↔ ... per the Kourovka files' idiom.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical core Prop `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRelativelyFree G → Monoid.IsTorsion (commutator G) → Monoid.ExponentExists (commutator G)` with the same bespoke `IsRelativelyFree` (generating set X with every map X → G extending to an endomorphism). I verified: `commutator G = ⁅⊤,⊤⁆` is G'; `Monoid.IsTorsion ↥(commutator G)` unfolds to 'every element of G' has finite order' (periodic); `Monoid.ExponentExists ↥(commutator G)` unfolds to '∃ n > 0, ∀ g, g^n = 1' (finite exponent); `answer(True)` is the positive answer and the RHS is a fixed Prop that constrains the answer. The bespoke definition is equivalent to 'free in some variety': (⇒) universal property with target G ∈ 𝔙; (⇐) for F = F(X) ↠ G every hom F → G factors through an endomorphism of G, so ker π = ⋂ ker(F → G) = V(F) for 𝔙 = var(G). Rank is unrestricted (X : Set G arbitrary); degenerate rank 0/1 cases satisfy the conclusion trivially and do not distort the statement. c08 chosen as the base because it uses `Type` (repo idiom in Kourovka/1_40, 19_25, 20_76; also mathematically safe since the properties depend only on the variety via finite-rank retracts), includes the API lemmas CONTRIBUTING asks for with bespoke definitions (`category API`, unlike c07's `category test`), and has concise docstrings. Only edit: wrapped one 103-character line to satisfy the 100-column style lint. c02/c03 differ by using `Type*` in the theorem (universe-polymorphic; not wrong but off-idiom); c03/c04/c06 lack API lemmas.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.21

by L. G. Kovács

If the commutator subgroup $G'$ of a relatively free group $G$ is periodic, must $G'$ have
finite exponent?

A group is *relatively free* if it is free in some variety of groups. Equivalently, it has a
generating set $X$ such that every map $X \to G$ extends to an endomorphism of $G$
(H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1). No restriction is placed on the rank of $G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.21»

/--
A group $G$ is *relatively free* (that is, free in some variety of groups) if it has a
generating set $X$ such that every map $X \to G$ extends to an endomorphism of $G$.
-/
def IsRelativelyFree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Set G, Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ f : X → G, ∃ φ : G →* G, ∀ x : X, φ x = f x

/-- Free groups are relatively free. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_freeGroup (α : Type*) : IsRelativelyFree (FreeGroup α) := by
  refine ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, fun f => ?_⟩
  refine ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun a => f ⟨FreeGroup.of a, a, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨_, a, rfl⟩
  simp

/-- The trivial group is relatively free. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsRelativelyFree G :=
  ⟨∅, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun _ => ⟨MonoidHom.id G, fun x => x.2.elim⟩⟩

/--
If the commutator subgroup $G'$ of a relatively free group $G$ is periodic, must $G'$ have
finite exponent?

Here "periodic" means that every element of $G'$ has finite order, and "finite exponent"
means that there is some $n \geq 1$ with $x^n = 1$ for all $x \in G'$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRelativelyFree G →
      Monoid.IsTorsion (commutator G) → Monoid.ExponentExists (commutator G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.21»

items: 'Relatively free' is formalized via the endomorphism-extension characterisation (generating set X with every map X → G extending to an endomorphism) rather than by constructing varieties/verbal subgroups and F/V(F). The two are equivalent by a standard argument (G is then free on X in var(G)), but a reviewer should confirm they accept this reading.
G ranges over `Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76); this still admits relatively free groups of every cardinality/rank, as the problem intends.

'Periodic' = `Monoid.IsTorsion ↥(commutator G)` and 'finite exponent' = `Monoid.ExponentExists ↥(commutator G)` (n > 0 with g^n = 1 for all g ∈ G'), applied to the commutator subgroup coerced to a group.

The bespoke definition lives in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean and 1_74.lean) rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib, since the task constrains all work to a single file; it could be moved to FormalConjecturesForMathlib if the maintainers prefer.
`answer(True)` corresponds to the positive answer ('yes, G' must have finite exponent'), `answer(False)` to the existence of a relatively free group with periodic G' of infinite exponent.

reviewer_notes: Statement is a single yes/no question; no ambiguity beyond the definition of 'relatively free', which has no Mathlib primitive. All candidates independently converged on the same standard equivalent characterization (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups), which I checked by hand in both directions. No candidate omitted the slot. Reference URL uses arXiv v46 (the cited source) whereas existing Kourovka files cite v40; kept v46 as instructed. Final file compiles under `lake env lean` with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning and all lines ≤ 100 chars.
